items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: He had Kenny Dorham in the band on trumpet.

ctx.x: But the trio lasted, I guess, about a year and a half, in which we played two or three clubs in Washington.

It was around late summer of 1947 that Billy Eckstine finally gave up his band, because the War was over and all the principal guys had left. And he had good men in his band. He had acquired tenor saxophonist Frank Wess. By this time Miles Davis was in New York, and he had Miles Davis in the band. He had Kenny Dorham in the band on trumpet. And Norris Turner [SIC: NORRIS TURNEY?], the alto saxophone player. I was trying to think of his name the other day, who played with the band. He was from Cincinnati. Norris…
